ACS my real blk people from Kentucky founded Liberia in the 1800s The American Colonization Society (ACS) was founded in 1816 in the United States with the goal of resettling free African Americans and freed slaves to Africa.

 The organization believed that Black people would have better opportunities for freedom and prosperity in Africa than in the racially discriminatory environment of the U.S. Key Figures: • Robert Finley, a Presbyterian minister, was one of the key founders. • Supporters included notable figures like James Monroe, Andrew Jackson, Henry Clay, and Francis Scott Key. Muhammad Ali was named after Cassius Clay who was Henry Clay cousin.

 Role in Liberia’s Founding: • In 1821, the ACS acquired land on the West African coast, which later became Liberia. • The colony was formally established in 1822, with the capital named Monrovia after President James Monroe, a supporter of the ACS. • 

Liberia declared its independence in 1847, becoming Africa’s first republic, largely populated by freed African Americans, known as Americo-Liberians. Many of the settlers brought with them American cultural practices, creating a complex dynamic with the indigenous African populations.
